messages.content:
Work out the ICD-10-AM principal diagnosis category for the episode below. The principal diagnosis is the single condition established after investigation to be chiefly responsible for the patient's episode of admitted care. It is not the patient's most serious comorbidity, not the presenting symptom, and not the procedure performed.

Think in three steps: first name the condition chiefly responsible for the admission, second name the ICD-10-AM chapter letter it belongs to, third give the three-character category.

Example 1
Hospital course: A 72-year-old man with a 50 pack-year smoking history was admitted with three days of worsening breathlessness and purulent sputum. Spirometry showed an FEV1/FVC ratio of 0.52. He was treated with nebulised bronchodilators, oral prednisolone and antibiotics for an infective exacerbation of his long-standing airflow limitation.
Answer: Irreversible airflow limitation in a heavy smoker with an infective exacerbation is chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, chapter J, category J44.
CODE: J44

Example 2
Hospital course: A 58-year-old man presented with crushing central chest pain radiating to the jaw. The electrocardiogram showed ST elevation in the anterior leads and high-sensitivity troponin rose from 40 to 2100 ng/L. He underwent primary percutaneous coronary intervention with a stent to the proximal left anterior descending artery.
Answer: ST elevation with a rising troponin and culprit-vessel stenting is an acute myocardial infarction, chapter I, category I21.
CODE: I21

Hospital course:
Discharge Summary:

Patient Name: [redacted]
Medical Record Number: [redacted]
Date of Discharge: [redacted]

Admission Date: [redacted]
Chief Complaint: Severe substernal chest pain and diaphoresis
Final Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Hospital Course:
The patient, a 38-year-old male with a past medical history of high blood pressure, high cholesterol, and HIV infection, presented to the ED with severe chest pain and sweating. He had been having intermittent chest pain for one month that was worsened by exercise and heavy lifting and was not relieved by medication.
The physical examination was unremarkable except for elevated levels of troponin-I and ST-segment elevation on ECG, suggesting an inferior wall myocardial infarction (IWMI). The patient was immediately transferred to the cardiac catheterization laboratory for an emergent coronary angiogram procedure, which revealed an LAD wrapped around the apex with 95% stenosis.
Balloon angioplasty was successfully performed, and a drug-eluting stent was placed in the 95% lesion of the LAD with minimal residual stenosis. The patient remained stable in the post-operative period and was discharged on aspirin, atorvastatin, metoprolol, enalapril, and ticagrelor, which were prescribed to manage his condition.

Hospital Course Summary:
The patient was admitted to the ED with severe substernal chest pain and sweating, which was diagnosed as an impending STEMI. After being treated with an emergent coronary angiogram procedure, balloon angioplasty, and a drug-eluting stent, the patient remained stable and was discharged with medications to control his condition.

Write your reasoning in at most three short sentences, then a final line of exactly 'CODE: <letter><digit><digit>'.

text:
Inferior ST elevation with a raised troponin and emergent stenting of a wrap-around LAD culprit lesion is an acute myocardial infarction. The HIV infection and high blood pressure are comorbidities, not the reason for this admission. Acute myocardial infarction belongs to chapter I, category I21.

CODE: I21
